newsitem.title: USA: Earthlink must raise cash to meet expenses.
newsitem.headline: Earthlink must raise cash to meet expenses.

text.p: Earthlink Networks Inc, an Internet service provider, Wednesday said its current cash is not enough to meet operating expenses for the rest of 1997.

In its 10-Q filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the company said it plans to raise additional cash from existing investors, institutional investors, strategic partners or by taking on additional debt.
At June 30, the company said it held cash and cash equivalents of $6.2 million versus a mere $1.2 million at the same time one year ago.
Earthlink had its initial public offering of stock in January at $13 a share. The stock closed Wednesday down 3/8 at 11-5/8.

In its filing, Earthlink estimated its capital expenditures will cost about $4.9 million through the remainder of 1997 for enhancing its computer networks, expanding its data center and other activities. In the second quarter ended June 30, capital expenses were $4.2 million versus $5.3 million in the same quarter of 1996.
The company reported a net loss of $5.3 million, or $0.80 a share, in the second quarter versus a loss of $5.9 million, or $1.04 a share, in the year ago quarter.
